items.title: Approval of the Minutes of February 28, 2023
Water Supply Conditions Update
items.text: Water Supply Conditions Update Steve Ritchie, Assistant General Manager (AGM) Water Enterprise, reviewed (1) March 6, 2023 Reservoir Storage: Hetch Hetchy is at 360,360-acre feet of maximum storage and Water Bank is at 100% of maximum storage; (2) Other California Reservoirs: Shasta is at 83% of historical average, Oroville is at 116% of historical average, and Don Pedro is at 104% of historical average; (3) California Drought Monitor; More areas of the state are out of drought; (4) Hetch Hetchy Precipitation: Tracking to the 1983 level; (5) Upcountry 6-Station Precipitation Index (as of March 4, 2023) Year-to-date (YTD) total is at 44.16 inches; (6) Bay Area 7-Station Precipitation Index (as of March 4, 2023) YTD total is at 33.51 inches; (7) Upcountry Snowpack: 180% of normal with additional snowpack received since report published; (8) Tuolumne River Water Available to the City: 711,000 acre feet; (9) National Precipitation Forecast: Additional rain and snow is expected in the coming weeks; and (10) Total Deliveries: 149 MGD with flat demand throughout the service area. AGM Ritchie discussed the Commission’s November 2021 Declaration of a Local Water Emergency which triggered a 5% drought surcharge for retail customers. He noted the Commission’s May 2022 adoption of an 11% Systemwide Water Use Reduction, consistent with the State Water Board’s Emergency Regulations. items.title: Audited Financial Statements (Fiscal Year 2021-22)
items.text: Audited Financial Statements (Fiscal Year 2021-22) Nancy Hom, Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and AGM Business Services, stated that on January 27, 2023 KPMG issued the Audited Financial Statement for Water, Wastewater, Hetch Hetchy Water and Power, and CleanPowerSF with (1) unmodified opinion, (2) no material misstatements in the financial statements, and (3) no internal control deficiencies observed. CFO Hom introduced Lisa Avis, Managing Director, KPMG, LLP. Director Avis thanked the SFPUC for their cooperation during the audit, which occurred in person and virtually and included daily communication with managers. She stated there were no audit misstatements, or uncorrected or corrected misstatements, and there were no fraud or illegal acts noted during the audit. She indicated that they are independent auditors and that they issued a clean and unmodified opinion. She stated that the opinion applies only to the SFPUC, although the wording “City and County of San Francisco” is used throughout the audit. items.title: Water Enterprise Capital Improvement Program Quarterly Report
items.text: Water Enterprise Capital Improvement Program (WECIP) Quarterly Report Katie Miller, Director Water Capital Programs, stated that as of December 31, 2022 the WECIP is 32% complete with $1,005 million expended during the quarter. She noted the WECIP cost summary by category for active projects. She reviewed new variances for the quarter, offering reasons for the variances and indicating they are monitored for trends and patterns. She stated the variances align with the revised project budget and schedules which were approved by the Commission in February. Director Miller noted there are 25 approved Regional projects in various stages, and those with cost and schedule variances are in the planning stage. Director Miller provided updates on Regional WECIP projects including the Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant Ozone, Sunol Long Term Improvements Watershed Center (Contract B), Harry Tracy Water Treatment Plant Filter Underdrain Replacement, and Corrosion Control. Director Miller provided detail on the 11 Local Projects and reviewed project budget and schedule variances, again stating the variances align with the revised project budget and schedules which were approved by the Commission in February. Director Miller provided updates on Local WECIP projects including San Francisco Westside Recycled Water, College Hill Reservoir, and Emergency Firefighting Water System Pipelines. items.title: Approve a form Master License for Outdoor Distributed Antenna System Pole Installation for placement of pole-mounted wireless facilities on streetlight poles owned by the SFPUC
items.text: Approve a form Master License for Outdoor Distributed Antenna System Pole Installation (2023 Master License) for placement of pole-mounted wireless facilities on streetlight poles owned by the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission; and delegate authority to the General Manager to execute the 2023 Master License and Pole License agreements allowing wireless telecommunications providers to install facilities on SFPUC poles. Barbara Hale, AGM Power Enterprise, summarized the requested approval action and provided a brief background of the Outdoor Distributed Antenna System Pole Installation Program which began in 2014. She discussed a 2018 Federal Communications Commission (FCC) decision which limited the amount of license fees that state and local governments could impose on telecommunications carriers for use of streetlight poles in the public right-of-way. She noted that appropriate City agencies worked together on the Master License Agreement (MLA), which is FCC compliant (rates and practices). She stated the five existing Master Licenses will remain in effect until expiration. She stated the proposed MLA modifies the permit and activity fees schedule to ensure cost recovery and will require the carriers to pay the new rates and fees for new installations. AGM Hale mentioned that the agenda item contained an error indicating that Mobilitie was included.
